rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
ΔT_b = K_b m
π = CRT
Δp/p = x₂ (Raoult)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ treat "Types of solutions" as one blob → ✅ split into: types of solutions, expression of concentration.  ·  ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Colligative properties depend on number of solute particles: relative lowering of vapour pressure Δp/p = x₂ (Raoult).  ·  Boiling-point elevation ΔT_b = K_b m; depression ΔT_f = K_f m; osmotic pressure π = CRT (dilute).

rows.text: Trick 1: Nine solution types reduce to a 3×3 grid (solute gas/liquid/solid × solvent gas/liquid/solid) — quote two examples: air (gas in gas), brass (solid in solid).  ·  Trick 2: Concentration conversions — mole fraction x = nA/(nA+nB); molarity M = moles/L solution (temperature-dependent); molality m = moles/kg solvent (temperature-INDEPENDENT, the exam favourite distinction).
